questions.q: What problem does the book say managers face when they make all decisions themselves?
a: They become the bottleneck through which all projects must go
They lose their ability to think creatively
They develop burnout from physical exhaustion
They become disconnected from their employees
questions.why: The bottleneck lesson describes managers as the bottleneck through which all projects and decisions must go.

questions.q: Which two questions does the book recommend starting most coaching sessions with?
a: What's on your mind? and And what else?
What's the real challenge here? and What do you want?
How can I help you? and What was most useful for you?
What do you want? and If you're saying yes, what are you saying no to?
questions.why: The right questions lesson says to start with the first two questions when beginning most coaching sessions.

questions.q: Why does the book advise asking what questions instead of why questions?
a: Because why can make people feel they need to defend themselves
Because what questions are always easier to answer
Because why questions are considered rude in most workplaces
Because what questions produce longer, more detailed responses
questions.why: The how to ask lesson explains that digging for reasons makes people feel they need to defend themselves.

questions.q: What does the book recommend as the first step when asking coaching questions?
a: Let employees relax by only asking one question at a time
Start with a theoretical question to warm them up
Ask multiple questions at once to save time
Begin by explaining why you are asking the question
questions.why: The how to ask lesson states the first step is to let employees relax by only asking one question at a time.

questions.q: According to the book, what is a common problem in workplaces and schools?
a: They lack the coaches and leaders people need to succeed
They have too many coaches causing confusion
They focus exclusively on technical skills over character
They require employees to have formal coaching certifications
questions.why: The overview states too many workplaces and schools are lacking the necessary coaches and leaders.
